description: Regression: minlength/maxlength count Unicode code points, NOT UTF-16 code units. PHP (mb_strlen / preg_split('//u')) and Go (utf8.RuneCountInString) and the legacy server (Validation.php:468 preg_split('//u')) all count code points. JS used value.length, which counts each astral character (emoji, U+1F600) as 2 surrogate code units and diverged. Each emoji below is 1 code point but 2 UTF-16 units, so these boundary cases fail under the old UTF-16 counting and pass under code-point counting.

tests.description: maxlength 3, two emoji = 2 code points (<=3) valid; old UTF-16 count was 4 and wrongly rejected
minlength 5, three emoji = 3 code points (<5) invalid; old UTF-16 count was 6 and wrongly accepted
minlength 3, exactly three emoji = 3 code points (==3) valid
Mixed ASCII + emoji counted by code point. 'a' + 1 emoji = 2 code points
